title: Program State
definition: Program state is the information an execution model must retain at a particular step to determine permitted next behavior.
purpose: Make execution inspectable as a sequence of state transitions rather than an opaque result.
history: State-machine and abstract-machine models provide long-standing formal and pedagogical tools for describing computation.
mental_model: A trace is a series of snapshots: each instruction reads a current snapshot and produces the next one.
analogy: A board-game position resembles state because it constrains legal next moves; it fails when hidden runtime resources are omitted.
relationships: includes selected memory and control state
real_world_usage: Reproducing a failing sequence from initial conditions
common_mistakes: Including irrelevant physical detail in a beginner abstraction
industry_notes: Logs, traces, debuggers, and tests expose selected state because complete physical state is impractical.
ai_notes: AI may invent intermediate state; require a deterministic trace and compare every transition with defined rules.
interview_notes: Ask what minimum state is necessary to predict the next step in a tiny machine.
exercise_candidates: Complete missing states in a four-step execution table
lab_candidates: Trace initial, intermediate, and final states of a tiny machine
project_candidates: Persist an inspectable state history in the instruction simulator
